fde-sdlc-business-requirement/fde-role-e.summary: Forward Deployed Engineers align customer problems with deliverable software through discovery, design, build, and handover.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
A **Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE)** combines engineering with customer delivery: clarify the problem, document scope, implement incrementally, validate with evidence, and hand over runnable artifacts.

**Typical sequence in this workshop:**

1. **Discovery** — stakeholders, constraints, success measures.
2. **Design** — UI flow and solution architecture.
3. **Development** — working software on localhost.
4. **MVP/POC** — repeatable run and pilot validation.
5. **Production** — hosted deployment and operations.
6. **Enterprise handover** — security, observability, and sponsor readout.


**Customer for Stages 3–9: a retail company (HQ and stores)**

- Approximately **50 employees** across stores and head office.
- IT receives **100 messages per week**; many repeat password, Wi‑Fi, VPN, and device questions.
- Answers exist in **~15 FAQ documents** (PDF or Word). Staff rarely read them.
- **IT lead (sponsor)** wants an internal **Ask IT** page: typed question, cited answer from FAQs, or a clear escalation to IT.
- One **restricted FAQ** (“Admin-only IT notes”) must not appear in answers for standard staff. Only **admin** role may retrieve content from that source.
- **Phase 1 scope:** FAQ assistant only—not a full ticketing or HR system.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body:
1. Review the retail case above.
2. Write one sentence describing the business problem.
3. Write one sentence describing measurable success for the IT lead.

sections.heading: Pitfalls
sections.body:
- Opening with technology choices before scope is agreed.
- Skipping written notes after stakeholder conversations.
- Expanding scope beyond the FAQ assistant in phase 1.

objectives: State the retail IT problem in one sentence

fde-sdlc-business-requirement/running-di.summary: Structured questions covering problem, users, FAQ sources, restricted content, and success metrics.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
Run a **30–45 minute discovery** with the IT lead. Capture answers under five headings:

1. **Current state** — how employees obtain IT answers today.
2. **Users** — who will use Ask IT (all staff, stores only, etc.).
3. **Knowledge base** — location, format, and count of FAQ documents; update process.
4. **Restrictions** — documents or topics that must not appear for standard staff.
5. **Success** — metric the sponsor will use (for example, reduction in repeat FAQ emails).

Send a short confirmation note after the session: “This is what we understood—please correct any errors.”

sections.heading: Example: Retail case
sections.body:
- Volume: ~100 IT emails weekly; high repetition on access and device topics.
- Users: ~50 employees; IT lead owns FAQ maintenance.
- Restricted FAQ: admin-only file; must not surface for staff role.
- Success: measurable drop in repeat FAQ-style emails within two months.

sections.heading: Template
sections.body:
```
DISCOVERY NOTES
Problem:
Users:
FAQ sources:
Restricted content:
Success metric:
Open questions:
```

objectives: Draft at least eight specific questions
checkpointQuestions: Why confirm notes with the sponsor?

fde-sdlc-business-requirement/writing-a-.summary: Goal, users, in-scope and out-of-scope items, and a measurable success criterion on a single page.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body:
The **BRD** is a one-page agreement: what will be built, what will not, and how success is measured. The IT lead should review it in about five minutes.

**Required sections:** goal, users, in scope, out of scope, success metric, open questions, approval line.

**Phase 1 in scope (retail case):** Ask IT page, answers from approved FAQs with source file name, refusal when no match, role-based exclusion of admin-only content.

**Out of scope (examples):** full ticketing, automated email replies, mobile-native app, company SSO integration.

sections.heading: Template
sections.body:
```
RETAIL — ASK IT (BRD v1)
Goal:
Users:
In scope:
Out of scope:
Success metric:
Approved by: ______  Date: ______
```

fde-sdlc-business-requirement/northwind-.summary: Run discovery against the retail case, then produce notes and a one-page BRD.

sections.heading: Procedure
sections.body:
1. Conduct a structured discovery session (partner or scripted sponsor).
2. Produce half a page of discovery notes.
3. Draft the one-page BRD from the template.
4. Peer review: can a reader understand scope without verbal explanation?

sections.heading: Pitfalls
sections.body:
- Missing out-of-scope section
- No success metric

objectives: Discovery notes and BRD v1 complete

fde-sdlc-business-requirement/ai-assista.summary: Respond professionally when the sponsor requests an AI assistant over internal documents.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body: Lead with discovery questions and a written scope summary—not infrastructure details.

sections.heading: Example: Retail case
sections.body: "I would confirm the business problem, intended users, document locations, any restricted sources, and how success will be measured. I would capture that in a one-page BRD and agree on a first deliverable: the Ask IT FAQ assistant before any ticketing expansion."

objectives: Cover users, data, restrictions, and success
typeExtras.prompt: The IT lead wants AI over internal IT FAQ documents. What do you do in the first 30 minutes?
